In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of a relativistic quark-level approach to the calculation of properties of cold neutron stars, with a particular interest in the prediction of the maximum mass and radius.
the study of the structure of cold neutron star matter and their properties in the context of a new density dependent effective nucleon-nucleon interaction.
the study of cold neutron star matter, in the framework of a relativistic, quasiparticle model of the nucleon, based on a density-dependent effective interaction derived from the QMC approach.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the QMC model is able to reproduce the main properties of cold neutron stars with an accuracy similar to that of more traditional approaches.
the QMC EOS provides a very promising description of the properties of high density neutron-star matter and of cold, slowly rotating stars.

the QMC EOs is able to provide neutron-star models in excellent agreement with the available observational data, with a maximum mass in the 1.9-2.1 M ⊙ range and with a maximum central density of 6 n 0.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the QMC Eos offers a consistent description for the properties of cold matter at high densities and for cold, slowly rotating, compact stars.

the QMC model provides a consistent description of cold neutron stars with a maximum mass in good agreement with the recent observations, and that this model is also able to describe finite nuclei, finite nuclei embedded in a nuclear medium, as well as the properties of cold, high-density matter in the core of neutron stars.
the quark–gluon structure of the hadrons is relevant for the description of cold matter and neutron stars.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a consistent relativistic description of nuclear matter at all densities and the quark–gluon level is possible and that it offers an attractive framework for the description of cold neutron stars and their properties.
the QMC model provides a realistic description of neutron-star matter, in agreement with the current observational data.

the QMC model, which is a self-consistent, quark level approach, is able to reproduce the main features of cold neutron stars with a realistic EoS, without the need of introducing additional parameters.
